key_insight: KMed-31B combines task-specific medical specialists into one model, improving clinical dialogue benchmarks while maintaining or slightly improving medical multiple-choice scores.
clinical_relevance: The approach targets institutions seeking on-premises medical AI, but benchmark gains do not establish safety or effectiveness in patient care.
method: Divide medical tasks into four categories by expected output and available feedback.
Train a specialist for each category and integrate them using Multi-teacher On-policy Delta Distillation (MOPD²).
Build Synthetic Health Dialogue from simulated patient–clinician consultations spanning common primary care presentations.
evidence_signal: Relative to its base model, thinking-mode HealthBench Hard rose from 23.80 to 51.48 and Professional from 41.97 to 59.18; four medical multiple-choice benchmark scores were maintained or slightly improved.
watch_item: The abstract reports benchmark evaluation rather than prospective clinical validation and does not quantify hardware requirements for on-premises deployment.
